prompt: Ellen wants to decorate the butterfly using these 6 stickers. Which butterfly can she make?

solutions.title: Use exactly the stickers
solutions.body:
The 6 stickers are 2 small light circles, 2 black ovals and 2 big dark circles. Each butterfly uses 6 stickers, so it must use exactly these: one small light circle, one oval and one big dark circle on each side.

Only butterfly A shows exactly 2 big dark circles, 2 small light circles and 2 black ovals. Each of the others uses a sticker Ellen has too many or too few of.

**Answer: (A)**

prompt: Into how many pieces will the string be cut?

solutions.title: Count the cuts
solutions.body:
Follow the dashed cut line and count where it crosses the string: it crosses 8 times. Each cut makes one more piece, so a string cut 8 times falls into $8 + 1 = 9$ pieces.

**Answer: (E) 9**

prompt: How many blocks are missing in this igloo?

solutions.title: Row by row
solutions.body:
Go through the rows of bricks that have a hole and count the missing bricks in each row, using the rows above and below to see where the brick joints are. Adding the missing bricks of all rows gives 10.

**Answer: (C) 10**

prompt: This picture shows a bracelet with pearls. Which of the bands below shows the same bracelet as above?

solutions.title: Follow the pearls
solutions.body:
Go around the bracelet and write down the order of the white and black pearls. A bracelet can be turned and flipped, so the same order may start anywhere and go either way round.

Compare this order with each band. Only band E has the pearls in the same order around the circle.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: Four of the numbers 1, 3, 4, 5 and 7 are written into the boxes so that the calculation □ + □ = □ + □ is correct. Which number was not used?

solutions.title: Even total
solutions.body:
Both sides are equal, so the four numbers used add up to twice one side: an even number.

All five numbers add up to $1 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 7 = 20$, which is even. To keep the total of the four used numbers even, the number left out must be even. The only even number is 4.

Check: $1 + 7 = 3 + 5$. ✓

**Answer: (C) 4**

prompt: Jim and Ben are sitting in a ferris wheel (see picture). The ferris wheel is turning. Now Ben is in the position where Jim was beforehand. Where is Jim now?

solutions.title: Same turn for both
solutions.body:
The wheel has 6 gondolas. Ben is at the top (12 o'clock) and Jim is at the lower left (8 o'clock).

Ben moves from 12 o'clock to 8 o'clock: that is 2 gondola places anticlockwise. Jim turns the same amount, from 8 o'clock to 4 o'clock: the lower right.

**Answer: (C)**

prompt: Alfred turns his building block 10 times. The first three times can be seen in the picture. What is the final position of the building block?

solutions.title: Find the repeat
solutions.body:
Look at the pictures: each turn is a quarter turn in the same direction, so after 4 turns the block is back where it started.

10 turns are $4 + 4 + 2$ turns, so the block ends up in the same position as after 2 turns. Find the option that matches the picture after turn 2: it is D.

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: In which picture are there half as many circles as triangles and twice as many squares as triangles?

solutions.title: Count each picture
solutions.body:
Count circles, triangles and squares in each picture. We need, for example, 1 circle, 2 triangles and 4 squares (circles = half of the triangles, squares = double the triangles).

Only picture E has this: twice as many triangles as circles and twice as many squares as triangles.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: Leo and Max are standing in a queue that is made up of 11 people in total. There are 7 people in front of Leo, Max stands directly behind him in the queue. How many people are behind Max?

solutions.title: Find the places
solutions.body:
7 people are in front of Leo, so Leo is 8th. Max is 9th. Behind Max are $11 - 9 = 2$ people.

**Answer: (B) 2**

prompt: Old McDonald has a horse, two cows and three pigs. How many more cows does he need, so that exactly half of all his animals are cows?

solutions.title: Cows = other animals
solutions.body:
Half of the animals are cows when there are as many cows as other animals. The other animals are 1 horse and 3 pigs: 4 animals. So he needs 4 cows, which is $4 - 2 = 2$ more.

Check: 4 cows out of 8 animals. ✓

**Answer: (C) 2**

prompt: Every box shows the result of the addition of the numbers on the very left and on the very top (for example: 5 + 7 = 12). Which number is written behind the star?

solutions.title: Find the missing number
solutions.body:
The box with 14 is ? + 10, so ? = 4. The star is ? + 7 = 4 + 7 = 11.

**Answer: (B) 11**

solutions.title: Compare columns
solutions.body:
In the first row, going from the 10 column to the 7 column takes away 3 (15 → 12). The same happens in the second row: $14 - 3 = 11$.

**Answer: (B) 11**

prompt: Lisa has several sheets of construction paper like these two kinds. She wants to make 7 identical crowns like the one shown. For that she cuts out the necessary parts. What is the minimum number of sheets of construction paper that she has to cut up?

solutions.title: Count the parts
solutions.body:
A crown is 1 bar, 4 dots and 1 plus. For 7 crowns she needs 7 bars, 28 dots and 7 pluses.

The first kind of sheet has 2 bars, 1 dot and 1 plus. The second kind has 5 dots and 3 pluses. Bars are only on the first kind, so she needs at least 4 of them (3 sheets give only 6 bars). These give 4 dots and 4 pluses.

She still needs $28 - 4 = 24$ dots. 4 sheets of the second kind give only 20 dots, so she needs 5 (25 dots, and plenty of pluses).

Altogether $4 + 5 = 9$ sheets.

**Answer: (B) 9**

prompt: Simon has two identical tiles, whose front looks like the picture. The back is white. Which pattern can he make with those two tiles?

solutions.title: Split into two tiles
solutions.body:
Each tile is an S-shape of 4 squares (2 on top, 2 below, shifted by one). On the front exactly one square is black: one of the two middle squares where the top and bottom rows overlap. The back is all white.

Pattern A: the left 2 bottom squares with the 2 top squares above them to the right form one S, with the black square in the middle position. The right half forms a second identical S, also with its black square in the middle position. So A works.

In the other patterns you cannot split the shape into two S-shapes that each have their black square in a middle position (for D, a 2 × 4 rectangle cannot even be split into two S-shapes, because its corners cannot be covered).

**Answer: (A)**

prompt: A kangaroo always does ten jumps within a minute. Then he has a three minute break. How many minutes does it need in order to do 50 jumps?

solutions.title: Jumps and breaks
solutions.body:
50 jumps take $50 \div 10 = 5$ jumping minutes. Between the 5 jumping minutes there are 4 breaks (no break is needed after the last jumps): $4 \times 3 = 12$ minutes.

Total: $5 + 12 = 17$ minutes.

**Answer: (D) 17**

prompt: Each one of the four keys locks exactly one padlock. Every letter on a padlock stands for exactly one digit. Same letters mean same digits. Which letters must be written on the fourth padlock?

solutions.title: Match the keys
solutions.body:
The padlocks show ADA, DGA, DAG and ?. The keys show 141, 717, 417 and 471.

DGA and DAG start with the same letter, so they belong to two keys starting with the same digit: 417 and 471. So D = 4.

ADA has the same first and last digit with D = 4 in the middle: 141. So A = 1.

DAG has A = 1 in the middle: 417, so G = 7. Then DGA = 471. ✓

The last key 717 is G, A, G.

**Answer: (D) GAG**
